item.description:
More accurate transcripts

  • Recordings are now transcribed in one pass. Loka was keeping the live text that scrolls past during a meeting, which is produced under a real-time constraint. It now re-transcribes the finished audio with the full-file decoder: about 5% more words recovered, and roughly three times faster than the old path.
  • Speakers stop getting merged. A clustering bug in the speech engine was collapsing distinct voices into one. Upgraded to the fixed version, and Loka now tells the diarizer how many people to expect when the meeting has an attendee list.
  • Transcript lines follow the conversation. Lines are split on real pauses rather than fixed windows, so a paragraph is a thought instead of an arbitrary 30-second slice.

Model picker

  • The recommended model is listed first, and models that scored badly in testing are labelled as such instead of sitting unmarked next to the good ones.

Under the hood

  • Loka is now an Apple Silicon build. The Intel slice could never run the summariser - the on-device model framework has no Intel backend - so it was removed rather than shipped broken.

More accurate transcripts

  • Words the recogniser reliably mishears are now corrected automatically. "Claude" was coming out as "clawed", "ClickUp" as "click up". Loka ships with correction rules for these, and they appear in Settings → Vocabulary where you can edit or remove them like your own.
  • Add your own corrections for names, products and shorthand specific to you - colleague names are the most valuable thing to add.

Easier-to-read transcripts

  • Transcripts get a readability pass after your notes are ready - punctuation and capitalisation added, filler removed. It runs quietly in the background and never delays your summary.
  • Your original words are always kept underneath. If the tidy-up is ever unsure about a line, that line stays exactly as it was spoken.

Under the hood

  • Dependency versions are now pinned, so transcription and summarisation behave consistently between updates.

Readable summaries

  • The summary is no longer one unbroken wall of text. Long meetings were producing a single ~300-word block with no paragraph breaks, in both note.md and the Summary tab. Summaries are now split into balanced paragraphs at sentence boundaries.
  • Short summaries are left alone - they read fine as one paragraph, and breaking them up would look arbitrary.
  • Splitting only ever inserts breaks. No wording is changed, reordered, or dropped.

Better notes on long meetings

  • Work nobody claimed is no longer thrown away. On longer meetings, tasks the group agreed needed doing but nobody volunteered for are now captured and shown as Unassigned, instead of being silently dropped. On a real 84-minute workshop this took action-item extraction from 3 candidates to 23.
  • The whole-meeting outline now scales with meeting length. It previously sampled a fixed amount regardless of how long the meeting was, so coverage got worse the longer you talked. An 84-minute workshop went from 3 outline sections to 7, and the topics got correspondingly more specific.
  • A speaker's thought is never split across two chunks. Chunks are now packed from whole speaker turns.

Cleaner output

  • Garbled speech no longer reaches your open questions. Unreadable transcription fragments are filtered out.
  • New "Worth checking" section. Flags actions with no owner, questions with no follow-up, and decisions with nothing implementing them. It only reports what it can prove from the summary itself - it never claims something wasn't discussed.
  • Dates from before the meeting no longer leak in, including written forms like "June 28".
  • Phantom speakers can no longer be named after a real person, so nobody gets added to a meeting they were never in.

Memory and disk

  • Fixes memory exhaustion on long meetings. The GPU buffer pool was effectively unbounded, so every discarded cache stayed resident for the whole meeting. This was the real reason an 8B model could run a machine out of RAM.
  • Retired model weights are reclaimed automatically in the background. Freed 31 GB of a 34 GB cache on the dev machine. No settings to change.
  • Newer Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 models are selectable. Qwen3-8B stays the default - it measured better for meeting notes than the newer families.

Reliability

  • One malformed field no longer destroys an entire summary.
  • Updated the speech engine to FluidAudio 0.15.5.

0.1.11

  • Frees the summarisation model's GPU memory after each summary, reducing resident memory
  • Mic loudness filter: drops audio picked up from distant speakers/other people so it doesn't pollute your side of the transcript
  • Shows your microphone's Voice Isolation status with a hint when it's off
  • Find in transcript (Cmd+F) with match navigation
  • Reordered the meeting tabs to Summary, Transcript, Notes, Speakers

0.1.10

  • Fixed transcription failing with a Core Audio error when a recording was damaged or incomplete
  • Meetings where one channel is unusable now still transcribe the channel that recorded correctly
  • Clearer messaging when a recording genuinely contains no audio

0.1.9

  • Action items are now attributed to the person who actually committed to them, not whoever the task is for
  • Due dates are computed correctly from spoken weekdays ("I'll jump on it Monday") and can no longer fall before the meeting date
  • Invented dates are scrubbed from summary text
  • Near-duplicate action items are merged; fabricated decisions no longer appear
  • "Speaker 1/2" labels no longer leak into note prose
  • More consistent structured extraction from the on-device model

0.1.8

  • Recording starts instantly now. Previously the Start button sat on "Preparing model..." while Parakeet warmed up; that's gone. Click Start, audio capture begins immediately, the live transcript catches up after the model is up (no audio is lost - the warmup buffers are queued and drained in order when ASR is ready).
  • Long monologues now break into paragraphs in the Transcript view. Pauses between speech automatically become paragraph breaks; rapid speakers without pauses get split at sentence boundaries. No more unbroken walls of text.
  • Version + Check for Updates in Settings. Cmd+, to General to see which build you're on and trigger an update check without having to dig through the menu bar.

0.1.7

  • New Transcript view. The Library Detail Transcript tab now uses speaker-grouped chat lanes - your voice in accent colour on the right, each meeting speaker in their own colour on the left. Much easier to scan than the old markdown wall.
  • Renaming a speaker now updates the summary too. Open a meeting's Speakers tab, type names, hit Save - the Transcript and Summary tabs (and note.md) both pick up the new names immediately. No more re-summarising just to swap "Speaker 1" for a real name.
  • Memory cleanup after every meeting. Once a recording finishes summarising, Loka releases the speech model and LLM weights instead of holding them resident forever. Next recording reloads them from disk cache (adds a few seconds to the Start button's loading step).
  • Fixed: saving speaker names from the Library window without first opening the menu bar popover surfaced an "Output folder isn't configured" warning.
  • Fixed: speaker names typed in the Speakers tab sometimes didn't appear in the transcript because of an internal id mismatch between FluidAudio's cluster labels and the synthesised "speaker_N" labels. Names now bridge both forms.

0.1.6

  • Loka now checks for updates the moment you open it, instead of waiting for the next scheduled 24-hour check.
  • Background check cadence reduced from 24 hours to 6 hours.

0.1.5

  • Tidied up the example text shown in the Vocabulary settings panel.

0.1.4

  • Echo cancellation is now automatically skipped when you're recording with headphones connected. Previously, playback volume dipped and Bluetooth headphones (like AirPods) dropped to mono call-quality audio while recording. Now headphones stay at full quality.
  • The Echo cancellation toggle in Settings still works as a master override.

0.1.3

  • Critical fix: 0.1.1 and 0.1.2 crashed at launch on macOS 26 (Tahoe) because the hardened runtime refused to load the bundled Sparkle framework. If you're on a previous version that won't launch, download this zip and drag it into Applications.

0.1.2

  • App icon - purple Loka glyph on a black plate. Visible in Finder, Dock, Spotlight, and the About panel.

0.1.1

  • Live transcript now appears almost instantly as italic hypothesis text and solidifies once confirmed. Previously the transcript was blank for the first ~10 seconds after each phrase.
  • Start recording shows a real loading state with a download progress bar while the speech model is being fetched on first use.
  • New meetings are named new-meeting by default (or new-meeting-2, new-meeting-3, etc.). After summarisation the meeting is automatically renamed to the title produced by the summary.
  • New Loka brand identity in the menu bar, onboarding, and app icon. The menu bar glyph turns red while recording, orange while starting and stopping.
  • Get Started in onboarding now actually closes the onboarding window.
  • Fixed: macOS no longer prompts for microphone permission repeatedly on first launch.

0.1.0 - First Sparkle release

Auto-updates are now wired up. Future versions will install in-place via the standard "Check for Updates..." menu item.

Headline features

  • Live recording pill with audio meter + meeting title
  • Floating transcript HUD + in-meeting notes editor
  • Notes-aware summarisation (Qwen3 14B by default)
  • Persistent speaker identity (voice embeddings)
  • Per-meeting and per-app audio capture scopes
  • Calendar-driven title + participant auto-fill
  • System notifications for pre-meeting, app-launch, and idle
  • Vocabulary terms + replacement rules
  • Rename + delete meetings from the library
